## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design runtime-extensible patterns, understand concurrency primitives, and execute safe zero-downtime swaps in production systems.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for pluggable eviction algorithms
- Registry pattern for runtime extensibility without restarts
- AtomicReference for thread-safe strategy swaps
- Per-shard isolation to prevent global bottlenecks and enable granular metrics

## Core Interface
```java
public interface EvictionStrategy<K,V> {
  void onPut(K key, V value);
  void onAccess(K key);
  K evictCandidate();
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle state migration when swapping eviction strategies at runtime?
- What are the performance implications of different eviction strategies?
- How would you implement custom eviction policies that require external coordination?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a pluggable, runtime-extendable auth system with strong tenant isolation, security, and observability. Demonstrates plugin loading, DI patterns, and security considerations critical at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Plugin architecture with dynamic loading
- Tenant isolation and per-tenant configuration
- Authentication flows: login, refresh, logout
- Security: short‑lived tokens, revocation, audit trails

## Code Example

```typescript
interface LoginRequest { provider: string; tenantId: string; credentials: any }
interface AuthResult { token: string; expiresAt: number }
interface AuthProvider {
  login(req: LoginRequest): Promise<AuthResult>
  refresh(token: string): Promise<AuthResult>
  logout(token: string): Promise<void>
}
interface ProviderFactory {
  create(tenantId: string, config: any): AuthProvider
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you version and hot-swap providers without downtime?
- How would you test provider isolation and revocation at scale?

## Why This Is Asked
Dynamic circuit-breaking with runtime rule extension is common in large-scale systems but hard to implement safely. This tests how a candidate balances performance, correctness, and distribution.

## Key Concepts
- Circuit-breaker state per endpoint
- Runtime registries and factories
- Distributed state and synchronization
- Testing concurrent trips and race conditions

## Code Example
```javascript
```javascript
interface CircuitBreakerRule {
  name: string
  shouldTrip(ctx: any): boolean
  onStateChange?(ctx: any): void
}
type RuleFactory = () => CircuitBreakerRule
class Registry {
  private map = new Map()
  register(name, factory){ this.map.set(name, factory) }
  create(name){ const f = this.map.get(name); return f ? f() : null }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you persist circuit-breaker state across a cluster?
- How would you test time-based thresholds and backoff without slowing tests?
